speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Women face barriers to full and equal participation in public life, including employment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Between 2012 and 2013, AWARE conducted a survey among 1,322 respondents as part of the We Can!

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Campaign, which aims to change societal attitudes that perpetuate violence against women.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The survey revealed that 52% of men think women are still expected to be in charge of caregiving and household chores.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Interestingly, the popularity of this view increased to 58% among men aged 18 and 29.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is worrying and I hope that we can change this mindset.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And perhaps, as many Members of this House have echoed the same view, it is time for us to review our maternity leave and paternity leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We might be reinforcing the mindset that women are in charge of caregiving when women receive a significantly higher amount of leave as compared to men.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this regard, I wish to highlight the endeavours made by the Young Women's Leadership Connection that has a variety of programmes to support young women leaders to fulfil their aspirations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I grew up with my sister Lynette and my two female cousins Gail and Grace.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I grew up with three girls and playtime usually meant Barbie time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Well, it was either playing with dolls or playing alone and so playing with dolls it was.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ken, the Barbie doll, became my best friend.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Fast forward 30 years and playtime now for me is back to playing with dolls with my daughter Ella.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have to stress that she chose playing with dolls, not me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And she is now bringing her dolls to the hospital to introduce them to her sisters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And so, I am sure when my twins Katie and Poppy become bigger, it is going to be more dolls.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ken is already on standby in my drawer.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: On behalf of our tripartite partners, I want to assure this House that we share their passion and commitment for Singapore women to fulfil their family and career aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: When I was at the NTUC, about 10 years ago, I visited Denmark.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: I spoke with the union leaders in Denmark.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: They told me that they were very proud of three achievements of Denmark women.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Three high: high education, high employment rate and high TFR of 1.7.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: But most of all, they enjoyed another high, the fourth high, which is its ranking on the Happiness Index.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Denmark has got one of the highest achievements in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: So, I asked them, "What is your secret to getting these highs?" They said that the women in Denmark receive very strong support from the government, employer, community, as well as from the husband.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: For example, it is socially unacceptable for husbands not to spend their weekends with the family.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Certainly, there is much we can learn from Denmark and we did.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Over the last 10 years, through the concerted efforts of the tripartite partners, we have made steady progress.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: If you were to compare our women employment with that of the OECD countries 10 years ago, we were ranked 23rd.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In other words, we have made progress from just outside the top 20, to just outside the top 10.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is similar to that for men, which is 5.5%.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In other words, the median wage gap between men and women has not widened further over the last 10 years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is faster than the growth rate of 7.7% for men and closes the gap in terms of average CPF balances between men and women, from 16% 10 years ago, to 11% last year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Eighty-two percent of employees in Singapore also work in firms that offer ad hoc flexible work arrangement, and this is up from 72% five years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The first area is to improve our female employment rate further.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Broadly speaking, the employment rate curve comes in three different shapes − single hump, double hump and no hump.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: So, our employment rate peaks at the age of 25 to 29, and declines thereafter.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is unlike the case of Japan and Korea where women re-enter the workforce from their mid-30s and they create a second hump in the employment curve at around age 50.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: So, Japan and Korea, they have the double hump.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is also unlike the case of the Nordic countries where women stay in employment for most of their adult life.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In other words, they do not leave and re-enter.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: They stay in employment for most of their adult life so forming a very high and broad inverted "U" − so, no hump.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Our challenge is: how can we help more women who are working today to stay in work and, at the same time, for those who have left, to return to work?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We will, therefore, have to increase our efforts to raise the adoption of flexible work arrangement for both employers and employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In fact, I was told that some employees hesitate to take advantage of FWA for fear of discrimination.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: And I think we have to change the mindset for both employers and employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In particular, we will give our strong support to NTUC on its Returnship Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We will also encourage companies to offer more part-time and job sharing opportunities for those who are not ready to go back to work on a full-time basis.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Under the Adapt and Grow initiative, we are doing more to help workers to learn new skills, to be more adaptable, so that they can keep pace with changes in the future economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is especially important for women who have taken a career break due to family commitment because, by the time they come back to work, the world may have changed due to disruption from technology, for example.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Some of them, even if they want to go back to the same career, they need to update their skill.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: So, there is a lot more that can be done.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: For some of them, maybe going back to their careers is no longer an option.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Therefore, there is a lot more that we need to do to support women, both in terms of helping them to stay in their current employment or to return to the same career or to take on a new career.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Members have made many good suggestions and this is certainly something that we will look into.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Thirdly, to enhance the retirement adequacy of Singapore women.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The transfer of CPF savings between spouses is a personal decision.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: I think it should be left to the couple to decide.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: It would be, I think, intrusive for the Government to mandate such transfers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: However, we do share Members' concerns about the spouses − whether they have adequate savings in their CPF for their retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: And what we have done is to relax the rules for spouses' transfers and the response has been positive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In fact, the amount doubled that of the year before.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In other words, more families, more CPF members are taking the step to transfer their CPF savings for their spouses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: And this is especially helpful for elderly women who were primary caregivers in their younger days.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Fourthly, to strengthen the HR practices for fair and equal treatment, regardless of gender.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Indeed, employers should set clear targets, conduct regular performance assessments and appraise employees fairly based on work outcome, regardless of whether these employees are on flexi-load, flexi-time or flexi-place work arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is advocated in the tripartite advisory on flexible work arrangements and further reinforced in the tripartite guidelines on fair employment practices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Of course, we are aware there are employers who do not observe these guidelines.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: So, for employees who feel discriminated against, TAFEP will look into their complaints and refer cases to MOM for action to warn them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: At the same time, I am happy to say that there are many employers who do provide a conducive and supportive environment for their female employees − from flexi-load at Shell to flexi-place at DBS and flexi-time at KPMG − just to name a few.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Our next challenge is to grow this community of progressive employers and make such practices a common sight in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: However, there is still much we can do.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: MOM, together with our tripartite partners, will study them carefully and incorporate them into the tripartite standards where relevant.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We should support them to fulfil their aspirations in both.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When Mdm Er reached school-going age, Mr Lee Kuan Yew emerged as the leader of a fledgling nation, then still seeking its independence from the British.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: He called on families to send their children − both boys and girls − to school, to forge the foundation of an educated and effective workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, unlike her older sister, Mdm Er and her younger sisters went to school with their brothers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, she is a fine example of lifelong learning because she kept attending classes to improve herself.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: She got better and better jobs over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: She was a cold chef preparing non-cooked food in Raffles Hotel and, later, was an executive chef with Singapore Food Industries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: With my extra money, I could give my four children a comfortable life." Was life easy?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I am sure it was not, but she worked hard with the opportunities afforded to her.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Men and women may have different perspectives, insights and instincts, but there is one clear constant.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But, Madam, the fact that we have this Motion in the first place says something.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This equality is still work-in-progress, but, thankfully, a work that remains very much alive and that builds on the achievements of our Pioneers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is a unique opportunity for us to also present an overview of how the Singapore Government values women in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My colleagues from MOM, MOE and MOH have also shared in greater detail the efforts being undertaken in their respective Ministries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We believe in helping every woman fulfil her potential and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To do so, we must ensure that the playing field is even and opportunities are fair between men and women.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the same time, we must also ensure that women have the right to choose and that we should respect those choices.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: How do we translate this vision into reality?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Well, we must, first, believe in the worth and potential of our people − both women and men.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Let us start at the beginning more than 50 years ago, when we laid the foundation for our women to progress.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The PAP's first election manifesto, "The Tasks Ahead", not only outlined its promises to build homes and schools, to reorganise the Civil Service and build a strong and united trade union movement, it also put across its policy on women's rights.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There was a strong desire to uplift our womenfolk in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Two of them, Chan Choy Siong and Ho Puay Choo, founded the PAP Women's League, the forerunner of today's PAP Women's Wing which is tabling the Motion today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As Mdm Er's story shows, education was a fundamental driver of change.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew said, and I quote, "The key is education.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Old-fashioned attitudes of teaching women enough to be literate and useful wives have undergone profound changes in the last 20 years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Societies which do not educate and use half their potential because they are women are those which will be worse off." So, we embarked on universal education for all children, regardless of gender.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Many of you would be familiar with this Charter as I had recently tabled amendments to it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Many of us actually take it for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: What we enjoy today, we forget where we came from.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But the Women's Charter was a powerful signal on how we viewed women in Singapore and how we were going to recognise and support them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have also made significant progress on the health and employment front.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This brings us from number 23 previously to number 12 now, compared to other OECD countries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our infant and maternal mortality rates are among the lowest in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Life expectancy at birth for females is 84.9 years − more than men.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have established strong foundations but we must build further on them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: First, we must eliminate barriers in the public sphere, be they in the workplace or in the community, to ensure that women reach their full potential.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Women have made and can make significant contributions to not only the economy, but also our society at large.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, it is important to remember that it is not just on the economic front and the economic value that we are looking at women.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There is also a broader value that women provide, along with men.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As a nation, we would be foolish not to value and to nurture them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Second, we need to make changes on the domestic front, in keeping with the changing realities of our modern times, to recognise the evolving roles for both men and women at home and in their personal relationships.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: How do we provide more options for our women and, also, men?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Like men, women are not a homogenous population with uniform preferences.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some prefer to focus on work, while others prefer to focus on family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our job is to respect these choices and work them within the larger collective aspiration.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We aim to put in place an environment that supports our women and men to be able to make these choices.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I emphasise that we must never trivialise choices made by fathers and mothers to spend more time with their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is invaluable both for the family and for society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For women, the need to balance career and familial commitments is usually more intense because of the way we view them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Others take a less linear career path to focus on their family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They exit the workforce, they come back again.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In doing so, they may find it difficult to return to the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: All these are real challenges, especially when you add on the economic uncertainties that we are facing today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Alex Yam, Miss Cheryl Chan, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Louis Ng, Ms Sun Xueling, Ms K Thanaletchmi, Mr Leon Perera and Mr Desmond Choo pointed out that flexible work arrangements are vital.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Minister Lim Swee Say has shared the range of efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Government has promoted and implemented flexible work arrangements and progressive work practices over the years and we must continue to keep up these efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, your suggestions and ideas are certainly valuable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This also includes the Tripartite Standards on Flexible Arrangements which MOM has introduced.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We want employers to offer these options to their employees.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is not good enough to present them and have them available but they must offer them to employees.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling argued for building capacity to help women juggle work and family priorities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Women who have taken a break from work to focus on their families may wish to return to the workforce after their children have grown up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Yet, they may find it difficult to start working again because, sometimes, after they exit the workforce, their skills may have "expired", especially at the rate at which technology is changing; some of us may become irrelevant.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Darryl David and Ms Rahayu Mahzam suggested having a customised SkillsFuture package to help these women update their skills to facilitate their return to the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung explained how we can and should offer guidance and support to help all the different groups to sieve out the relevant modules that are available.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We need to create more modules that may be applicable to the different segments of society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Indeed, a more user-centric approach would be useful.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will see how to do that better.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Working couples who have just started a family may also need support in caring for their young children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: On this front, as Members are aware, the Government has endeavoured to improve the quality, accessibility and affordability of preschool services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To increase accessibility, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has increased the number of childcare places island-wide, especially in estates with more young families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To support parents with childcare and infant care expenses and ensure affordability, all parents receive subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Additional subsidies are also available to the broad majority of lower and middle income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For non-working mothers who are retrenched, looking for jobs or undergoing training, we will consider their issues on a case-by-case basis, so that these subsidies are available to them as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah mentioned that working parents prefer to be near their young children during the work day.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To address this, Ms Tin Pei Ling suggested having more care facilities near workplaces.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: You will be pleased to know that ECDA has worked with URA to set up childcare centres in commercial developments under the Community and Sports Facilities Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Under this Scheme, the developers for selected Government Land Sale sites are also required to provide space for childcare centres.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some parents work shifts and may require childcare services in line with their working hours.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Sun Xueling suggested extending the operating hours of childcare centres.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Currently, they are required to operate full-day services from 7.00 am to 7.00 pm daily on weekdays to cater to the needs of most working parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some centres have chosen to extend their operating hours to better cater to parents' schedules.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Currently, there are already 52 centres offering extended operating hours island-wide.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Tin Pei Ling gave several thoughtful recommendations to better support those who are caring for their elderly family members.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Minister of State Lam Pin Min addressed some of these recommendations yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Caring for our elderly is a key focus of MOH in the years to come as we address the issue of ageing in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Thirdly, how do we facilitate women in terms of leadership positions in industries?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Much of the effort I have addressed and elaborated on so far deals with the career progression of our women.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As a country, and as an economy, we must not under-estimate the contributions that women can make at the apex of our corporates.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Louis Ng, Mr Leon Perera, Mr Vikram Nair, Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Tin Pei Ling agree that having women in corporate leadership makes good sense for businesses and the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Today, our women are well-educated and contribute actively to our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To address this, my Ministry set up a Diversity Action Committee (DAC) in August 2014 to build up women's representation on boards of companies listed on the Singapore Exchange and to expand the pool of board-ready women.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It comprises respected business leaders from the private sector like Singtel, CDL, Shell and IBM; entrepreneurial and professional firms; as well as representatives from the people and public sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: DAC has recommended that we enhance the Code of Corporate Governance (CG Code) to require listed companies to disclose their board diversity policy, including gender, and their progress towards achieving these objectives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: PAP Women's Wing and BoardAgender have made a similar joint recommendation to revise the CG Code to require companies to disclose their board diversity, including gender, in their annual reports, on a "comply or explain" basis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: BoardAgender is an initiative under the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations, which aims to facilitate greater awareness of the benefits of gender balanced business, as well as the advancement of women into senior leadership positions and the boardroom.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: MAS has formed a Corporate Governance Council to review the CG Code and we look forward to developments on this front.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I dislike the fact that Singapore ranks near the bottom behind other key developed markets like Australia and the UK in terms of women on boards, in fact, even behind our neighbouring countries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Other countries are progressing at a much faster rate.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Globally, shareholders and institutional investors increasingly view women on boards as being important for board effectiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is something that Singapore corporates should not ignore anymore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I appreciate the other joint recommendation by PAP Women's Wing and BoardAgender.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is timely and I support this target.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, DAC discussed the same issue at its recent meeting in February 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I want to see more women breaking the "glass ceilings" in the next few years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Beyond business, it is also very important for us to look at the non-profit sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Centre for Non-Profit Leadership and the Charities Unit have carried out an inaugural study on non-profit board leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The study shows that more women are represented on the boards of charities, compared with businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Helen Keller once said, "Life is an exciting business and most exciting when it is lived for others".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One sterling example is Mrs Leaena Tambyah, who retired as senior adviser to the Asian Women's Welfare Association (AWWA) in 2013 after many years of devoting her time and effort helping others, especially children with special needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Another example, is Mrs Thung Syn Neo, a social work pioneer, whose key contribution is the concept of the Family Service Centres that we have today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Women leaders in the non-profit sector have shown that a combination of "heart and mind" can go a long way in building up our social capital and help us to become a more caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While women sitting on the boards of these charities make up about 31%, 13% of the charities still have no female representation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My Ministry and the National Council of Social Service will look into this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I believe we can improve on this figure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While we provide support for women to balance their work-family commitments and excel in the business and non-profit sectors, we must not forget that there are also vulnerable groups of women who require more support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We must also help them to overcome particular barriers so that they, too, can realise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One such group is single mothers, which has been raised by Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Leon Perera, Mr Faisal Manap and Ms Joan Pereira.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some talked about singles, referred to divorcees, to unwed mothers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For us, we continue to support parenthood within marriage but, whatever the circumstances, we remain child-centric.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is important for us to do that.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Single parents' children get the same health and education benefits as any other citizen's child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have also made policy changes in recent years to provide more support for parents to support their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I have also highlighted several times in this House about KidSTART which will help parents who need support for the development of their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is an extensive effort that will not just focus on the children but also link families with community resources if they have other social and financial needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This programme precisely focuses on the groups that many of us here are concerned about.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I believe it will make a significant amount of difference.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Joan Pereira appealed to treat a single mother and her children as a "family nucleus" in HDB applications.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is very clear to us that housing is an important institution for children's well-being and development.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our housing policies aim to address the needs of the vulnerable without, at the same time, trying to undermine self-reliance, family support and parity with other families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Depending on their age, they may apply for HDB flats themselves, or jointly with their parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: On a case-by-case basis, HDB makes exceptions to help single parents, whether divorcees or otherwise, with their housing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Do surface their cases to us and we will look at them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While I specifically mentioned the Women's Charter earlier, something we often overlook is how our laws have also made Singapore a safer place for women.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is something we should not take for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is not something that women in other countries necessarily have.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the same time, we need to make sure that we have to shape society's ideas about what is not acceptable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Although married persons have conjugal rights over each other, such rights should be exercised within reasonable behaviour.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I believe that this is an important area where we can provide support for women to achieve their true potential.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think it is important for us to remember.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The first line of support must surely be the family and that is something that cannot be mandated, that is something that all of us can play a part.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Dr Intan Azura, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Leon Perera, Mr Darryl David and Ms Tin Pei Ling reminded us we need to have a cultural shift and a mindset change, especially about the share of care responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun also reminded us that eliminating gender stereotypes starts from young.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: What we do at home as mothers and fathers, husbands and wives is extremely powerful.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: By our example, we socialise our daughters and sons into their future roles when they set up their own homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We can either help them move with the times and evolve more appropriate interpretations, or we can unnecessarily confine and restrict their understanding of the roles and duties of mothers and fathers, and of husbands and wives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Even today, while women in Singapore enjoy equality in many aspects of society, including education and employment, the greater responsibility of caregiving within the family continues to fall on women.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We need to change the paradigm relating to the roles men and women play.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As husbands, fathers, brothers and sons, we should step up to play our part at home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Parenting responsibilities can and should be shared with our wives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Household chores should not be seen as only the purview of female family members, including the domestic helpers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: If the women around us continue to bear the disproportionate burden of family and caregiving responsibilities, it is less likely that they can achieve all that they are capable of.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Only 13% of the respondents said that the role of cooking was shared equally between spouses, while only 23% said that this role of feeding young children was undertaken equally by both parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We really need to begin walking the talk.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As husbands and fathers, it is important for us to share the household and parenting responsibilities with our wives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This would provide working women with the necessary support to alleviate the work-life conflict that they face.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Research also shows that this brings about stronger and happier marriages, as both parties better understand and feel supported in managing day-to-day chores and concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Stronger families mean a much better environment for our children to grow up in.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Studies have also shown that children with active fathers have better social skills, they do better academically and have less behavioural problems.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Fathers, themselves, are more fulfilled as they are no longer the distant breadwinner and they are able to develop close bonds and ties with their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Fathers can also tap on four weeks of shared parental leave, with effect from July this year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is available to both mothers and fathers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But only families can decide what steps to take.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We cannot walk that last mile for them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A 2013 survey on Social Attitudes of Singaporeans indicated that men are changing their attitudes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Fifty-eight percent of men in 2013, compared to 44% in 2009, said that their work demands ate into their family time more than they liked.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The point that more men are identifying a conflict between work and family commitments is also highlighted in the 2014 Employer Alliance survey, where men indicated an increasing desire to have flexible work arrangements so they can help out with the children and domestic responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Businesses must, therefore, realise that employees, including men, do not perform their best when they feel conflicted and are unable to juggle career and home demands.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Enlightened businesses know that when they help both fathers and mothers manage their work-life balance, they are the ones that will succeed in retaining talent and recruiting new talent.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, again, the survey looks positive but we need to really begin to walk the talk, across the board.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Members of this House will be familiar with the Dads for Life movement and the Centre for Fathering.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Many have asked me why is there not a Moms for Life movement or a Centre for Mothering.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Do they not have a role to play, too?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My response is that actually moms are already for life and mothers are already at the centre of everything!

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Playing the roles as we should, as husbands and fathers, will help level the playing field for women in so many ways.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The lives of women in Singapore have improved significantly over the years through the various Government policies and initiatives, as well as more enlightened societal perspectives and practices.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We must continue to remove the barriers faced by women in the public sphere.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: However, the fundamental societal change can never be achieved by the Government alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The change also needs to take place at home, in our workplaces and in our communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As Dr Aline Wong said in a book entitled "Our Lives to Live", "True equality lies in a woman's ability to realise her full potential and be her true self in whatever she endeavours to achieve." Let us endeavour to make this happen.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I am heartened that many Members of this House have stepped forth to speak passionately on this important cause, and our Ministers and Ministers of State have also given so much of their time to address our concerns, recommendations and, very importantly, echo their support for the aspirations of Singapore women.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And I certainly appreciate the interest and support from the Workers' Party and Nominated Members of Parliament in this Motion debate as well.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Through the debate, colleagues and I have articulated and elaborated on the four strategies that we believe are critical to supporting Singapore women in their aspirational pursuits.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As we have all agreed that as of the current reality, the primary caregiving role is undertaken by women.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Therefore, there is a need to give more support to our caregivers so as to free up the capacity to pursue their aspirations, whether it is in the social area or the career arena.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In this aspect, I am glad that colleagues, such as hon Ms Joan Pereira, Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin and Ms Sun Xueling, have all alluded to it in their speeches.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: At the same time, we also need to refresh and build new capabilities in our women to help back-to-work women because, with new capabilities or refreshed capabilities, when they skill up, they also build and create new capacity as well.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This was very passionately spoken about by hon Members Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Darryl David, Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The second strategy is to be able to provide options for women to choose.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We also talked about how this needs to be complemented by having progressive HR policies and practices in place.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This had been elaborated on and championed by hon Members Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Darryl David.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: For women who wish to focus our energies on family caregiving − to raise children, to take care of the elderly − there is often one thing that weighs very heavily on our minds and, that is, retirement adequacy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This was also something that our PAP Women's Wing had in the past raised, that is, top up with love.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, these are the key points that our Members of Parliament, my colleagues, have raised very passionately about in terms of providing options for women.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The third strategy is to remove barriers, to remove the invisible barriers that are often stereotypical, as well as pigeon-holing women in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: At the leadership level, we talked about how women have been under-represented at the board level, at the executive level, and also how we should also drive up women's participation and leadership within the community.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These have all been very passionately talked about by Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Sun Xueling, Mr Vikram Nair, Mr Alex Yam and Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But to do so, we also need to acknowledge, recognise the stereotypes, the biases that are constraining women in these different roles.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, it is very heartening to hear that various Members, such as Mr Darryl David, Mr Louis Ng, Dr Intan Azura Moktar, Mr Leon Perera and Mr Kok Heng Leun, talk about the need to shift the care burden, to have a more equal sharing of care duties between men and women, whether it is at the workplace, in the family or even within the social setting.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is something that I believe we need to continue to work on and endeavour to achieve a more equal sharing of care duties.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: At the same time, as what Ms Jessica Tan had also elaborated on, to be conscious of our unconscious bias so that from recruitment to selection, women will not be inevitably disadvantaged right from the get-go.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As we look to the future, as we move towards a smart nation, as we leverage on digital technology, as we leverage on the smart solutions, we look at a world of great possibilities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: For women to also exploit these, we need to look at STEM education to empower them, equip them, get them ready for the job opportunities in these new and exciting areas.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These are also what Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Thanaletchimi had talked about at great length yesterday and today.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We need to leverage more on technology to provide remote caregiving to enable flexible work arrangements so that we can create the capacity and provide the options that we have been talking about to help women to fulfil their different aspirations.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is something that we must continue to look into, whether it is to prepare our new digital generations through formal education or through SkillsFuture where we encourage and equip our women to take on IT courses so that they can raise their digital fluency skills and close that gender gap.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In this arena, it is important that we take a serious look at this.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank the various Ministries for the very strong encouraging responses so far.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: One thing that I thought was very encouraging was that the nursing profession had also taken the lead to adopt flexi-work arrangements so that our nurses are able to juggle their different roles in life very well.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Second, I would also like to thank Minister Ong Ye Kung who spoke on behalf of MOE.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We are very heartened that the Ministry will be customising the engagement to engage women more, to have a more user-centric way of engaging our workforce to help them through customised sets of courses and to help them to eventually, hopefully, match with real job opportunities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Third, to Minister Lim Swee Say, for MOM.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I am very heartened – and I believe all my colleagues are – that flexi-work arrangement is something that is on top of mind at the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: That there will be strong support through NTUC to offer returnship programme with something very exciting and many women will definitely look forward to it.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As well as strengthening HR practices, fair employment, the tripartite standards that the Minister spoke about, I think this is something that we are fully supportive of.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, these are all very encouraging to us and these are definitely relevant to the recommendations that we have put forth.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: All of these, taken together, demonstrate the willingness of the Government to support the aspirations of Singapore women.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I definitely look forward to the Ministries implementing these recommendations and we look forward to the good news very soon.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, I deeply appreciate this opportunity to discuss with my parliamentary colleagues on this Motion, which is to affirm the importance and strategies to support the aspirations of Singapore women.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Members have put forward many good suggestions with regard to the Motion.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: They are in line with the four strategies described in my speech.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: First, help free up caregivers so that they can better manage their multiple roles.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Second, promote flexible work arrangements so that women can achieve both family and career aspirations without having to trade off one for the other.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Third, encourage society and the private sector to value women's economic potentials and contributions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Fourth, encourage women to undergo technology skills training and be prepared for the digital era and the future economy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: More importantly, we all agree that we must have concrete actions to support Singapore women to balance their multiple roles and fulfil their familial and career aspirations.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I am especially moved by the positive response from the various Ministries.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These positive responses affirm women's contributions towards the family, society and country.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: What is even more encouraging is that the Ministers have responded positively to Members' suggestions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This will undoubtedly strengthen Singapore's foundation and help Singaporean men and women achieve their potential and be future-ready.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I hope the Ministries can implement these recommendations soon.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: (In English): Many, if not all, of the recommendations that my colleagues and I have put forth in this Motion apply to Singaporeans regardless of gender.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Our support for women and men to balance their multiple roles should help them reach greater heights in our economy, in various professions and in many diverse frontiers.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.55 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 5.37 pm until 5.55 pm.
